mstts:express-as.prosody: Have you ever wondered who you really are, beneath all the roles and stories you carry? Questions about identity and self-understanding have always sparked both curiosity and, sometimes, a little discomfort in all of us. Together, we’re about to step into a journey inspired by Alan W. Watts and his thought-provoking work, On the Taboo Against Knowing Who You Are. Here, Watts invites us to take a closer look at the paradoxes of self-perception—challenging those invisible lines that seem to separate each of us from the rest of the universe. He gently reveals how the idea of being a separate ego, cut off from everything around us, is actually something we’ve learned from our culture. And, as you’ll see, this belief often leaves us feeling isolated and confused. But what if we could see through that illusion? As we explore the roots of this deep-seated taboo, we’ll start to unravel the beliefs that have kept us from recognizing our true nature—our fundamental connection to all that exists. You and I will question the familiar stories we tell ourselves about who we are, what consciousness means, and the very nature of reality. Along the way, Eastern wisdom and modern science come together, offering fresh ways of seeing the world and ourselves. The boundaries between self and other, mind and body, begin to fade away, opening up a sense of belonging and freedom that’s hard to put into words. So, let’s walk this path together—towards a rediscovery of identity, not as something isolated, but as a vibrant part of the ever-unfolding cosmos. By the end, you might just find yourself looking at who you are—and what it means to be alive—in a whole new light.
